associations.rationale: The formal equality only computes the cardinality of ConstructedIndex as the sum of the three displayed numbers; it does not itself identify those indices with distinct irreducible representations.
The type only asserts the existence of an unspecified type Irrep with cardinality q^2-1; it does not say that its elements classify the irreducible representations discussed in the source.
The formal equality directly identifies the displayed total of the three constructed-family counts with the number of conjugacy classes, exactly the comparison made in the source.
This type constructs an indexed representation family but does not itself state simplicity, pairwise distinction, the family counts, or completeness.
The implication from isomorphism to equality of indices directly asserts that the constructed representations are pairwise distinct, as required by the source's count.
The formal conclusion directly asserts that every constructed family member is simple, matching the source's treatment of the constructed representations as irreducible.

This is a general exhaustiveness criterion conditional on a simple, pairwise distinct family having the displayed cardinality, so it formalizes the source's proof strategy rather than directly naming the constructed classification.
The theorem derives an equality of numerical counts from a conjugacy-class count hypothesis; it does not itself assert that every irreducible representation belongs to the constructed families.
The formal type directly says every simple representation is isomorphic to a unique member of the constructed family, exactly the source's conclusion that all irreducibles have been found.

The existential Wedderburn decomposition and its resulting cardinality are indirect structural and counting evidence; the displayed type does not identify its index with the constructed representation family.
The type directly gives a pairwise nonisomorphic exhaustive family of simple representations with q^2-1 members, matching the source's complete irreducible count.
The conclusion is the opaque predicate foundAllIrreducibles, whose displayed type reveals no definition connecting it to the source's count or exhaustiveness statement.
